citation: Boan (2025), CONCURRENT ENGINEERING PROCESS FOR ELECTRICAL ARCHITECTURE OF NANOSATELLITES PRELIMINARY PHASES
title: CONCURRENT ENGINEERING PROCESS FOR ELECTRICAL ARCHITECTURE OF NANOSATELLITES PRELIMINARY PHASES
modeling_scope: Preliminary-phase concurrent engineering workflow for a 16U nanosatellite, centered on electrical/EPS architecture. The workflow builds a common satellite and mission reference, system-level budgets, power budgets, mission modes, power profiles, ephemeris-derived energy flows, and an Opalis model of solar generator, battery, regulators, bus topology, and losses to support sizing, trade-offs, and energy-balance simulations.
mbse_language_method_tool: Model-Based Systems Engineering is mentioned as the digital engineering context, but no SysML language is reported. The method is concurrent engineering through CNES PASO using IDM-CIC for system/subsystem description and geometry, Simu-CIC for mission scenario and ephemeris generation, IDM-Power for mode-based power profiles, Opalis with Flows Manager for power-system simulation, plus IDM-View/IDM-Plot visualization and standardized/CCSDS-like files for interoperability.
robot_platform: 16U nanosatellite in low-Earth orbit; first system analyses selected an SSO orbit at low altitude between 500 and 600 km. The use case is an agile UV spectropolarimetry mission for 3D mapping hot stars' dynamic environment.
task_domain: Preliminary electrical architecture and EPS sizing for an agile nanosatellite science mission requiring repeated observations of more than 40 stars and energy feasibility across observation plans.
interface: Standardized file/model interfaces connect engineers and tools: IDM-CIC and Simu-CIC feed a common database; Simu-CIC outputs CCSDS-like orbital scenario files used by Opalis Flows Manager; IDM-Power converts IDM-CIC power budgets into temporal power profiles for Opalis.
feedback: Iterative simulation and design loop: define subsystem/orbital scenario, allocate power to modes, generate power profile and energy flows, run Opalis energy-balance simulations, then adjust series/parallel solar-cell and battery assemblies and compare technologies/architectures until satisfactory SOC and energy equilibrium are reached.
evaluation: The workflow is demonstrated on a specific 16U nanosatellite use case. CNES flight-dynamics experts reduce the annual observation plan to a representative 48-hour worst-case sun-illumination scenario; the paper reports power-budget tables, Opalis simulations for stable energy balance, EPS architecture trade-offs, final solar-generator and battery sizing, and a battery worst-case survival/no-illumination simulation using SOC thresholds.
rq_relevance: RQ1 partial: the paper provides a concrete preliminary-phase workflow for modeling a nanosatellite mission and EPS with system descriptions, power budgets, power profiles, energy flows, and an electrical architecture simulation model, but it is a single CNES use case and does not present a general reusable MBSE reference model or explicitly address minimal behavioral knowledge. RQ2 partial: the paper claims integrability/interoperability, rapid impact analysis, smooth data exchange, parallel trade-offs, and energy-feasibility outcomes from model/tool integration; it does not make explicit reliability or reproducibility claims. RQ3 partial: EPS simulations are used before physical development to validate energy feasibility and worst-case SOC margins, but no formal verification, IVV, test-procedure, or requirement-verification model is described.
claimed_outcomes: The process defines an adaptable and interoperable model, allowing mission changes to be studied almost instantly by regenerating ephemeris data and configuration changes to be compared easily.
A common database lets subsystem experts perform targeted analyses in parallel while taking subsystem evolutions into account and analyzing impacts quickly and efficiently.

Standardized file formats and tool interoperability enable subsystem experts to exchange data, communicate through engineering models, and use dedicated specialized tools while preserving input/output compatibility.

The simulation workflow supports electrical sizing of solar generators and batteries under worst-case/end-of-life/temperature/orbital constraints and supports trade-offs among battery cells, solar cells, regulator types, bus voltages, and architecture options.

The paper reports simulation-based validation of observation-plan feasibility in terms of energy stability and checks a survival/no-illumination battery scenario against minimum SOC margins. Reproducibility and reliability are not explicitly claimed as MBSE outcomes.
verification_validation_linkage: The linkage is simulation-based rather than formal V&V. The EPS model, power profile, and ephemeris-derived energy flows are used to validate energy feasibility of observation plans, demonstrate a stable energy budget with SOC behavior, and simulate a battery worst-case survival scenario with acceptable SOC thresholds. No explicit test procedure, IVV process, verification matrix, or EPS requirement-verification model is reported.
key_findings: The paper frames electrical architecture work as part of a concurrent engineering process in which a common technical reference for satellite description and mission supports system-level budgets and subsystem analyses.

IDM-CIC provides system/subsystem description, basic geometry, and power budgets; Simu-CIC provides mission scenario and ephemeris; IDM-Power generates temporal power profiles; Opalis models electrical architecture and runs power simulations.
The Opalis EPS model includes battery and solar-generator assemblies, power bus topology, regulators, losses, temperature effects, and solar/earth/albedo energy flows.

For the use case, CNES reduced a complex observation plan to a 48-hour worst-case illumination scenario for EPS sizing, then used simulations to compare solar-panel configurations and power architectures.

The final reported EPS architecture uses two solar wings of 20 AzurSpace 3G30A cells each, arranged as 5 parallel strings of 4 cells in series, and a Li-ion INR 18650 battery in a 2S8P assembly with about 180 Wh end-of-life storage.
The conclusion claims the workflow enabled sizing, trade-off studies, energy-stability feasibility checks, sensitivity analyses, and smooth multidisciplinary data exchange in preliminary phases.

quality.rationale: The assigned metadata provides a DOI, but the venue name/type is not reported in the paper text available here. The paper does not discuss limitations, threats to validity, or methodological validity problems.

evidence_quotes.claim: Paper objective and modeling scope cover needs analysis, power budgets, sizing, simulations, and tool interoperability.
evidence_quotes.quote: The objective of this paper is to describe the approach through the prism of an electrical architect, that contributes to needs analysis, realization of power budgets, system sizing and energetic simulations through a specific use case.

evidence_quotes.claim: Use case is a nanosatellite platform in LEO.
evidence_quotes.quote: The selected use case to illustrate this paper is a 16U nanosatellite operating on low-earth orbit its mission being the 3D mapping of hot stars dynamic environment by using ultraviolet spectropolarimetry measurements from space for the first time.

evidence_quotes.claim: Orbit context is SSO at low altitude.
evidence_quotes.quote: The first system analyses concluded that the best orbit for the mission is an SSO orbit at low altitudes (between 500 and 600 km).

evidence_quotes.claim: Concurrent engineering workflow uses a common technical reference and system-level budgets.
evidence_quotes.quote: The overall concurrent engineering approach consists in setting up a common technical reference (satellite description and mission), with the aim of producing system-level budgets (mass, power, centering/inertias, data, etc.) produced by the various subsystems experts/architects.

evidence_quotes.claim: Core tools for system and mission modeling are IDM-CIC and Simu-CIC.
evidence_quotes.quote: IDM-CIC: used for system description (at system and sub-systems level) and for system basic geometry definition. Simu-CIC: used for mission scenario definition and ephemeris generation.

evidence_quotes.claim: Electrical architect tasks include EPS budgets, sizing, trade-offs, and power simulations.
evidence_quotes.quote: As an electrical architect specifically, the objective of any project preliminary phase would be: To define preliminary power budgets, To pre-size solar panels and batteries, To perform technological trade-offs, To simulate the on-board power usage.

evidence_quotes.claim: EPS simulation requires a model of power subsystem architecture and energy flows.
evidence_quotes.quote: A model of the power sub-system: battery and solar generator assemblies, power bus topology, type of architecture, regulators, etc.

The tool includes precise modelling of electrical architectures including batteries, solar panels, regulators and bus topologies by taking into account the specific features of each element such as losses, temperature impacts, etc.

evidence_quotes.claim: Tool interoperability is based on standardized files and ephemeris conversion.
evidence_quotes.quote: The energy flows are generated by the Flows Manager plugin that is now included natively in Opalis. It takes the CCSDS-like standard files generated by Simu-CIC (orbital scenario description) as an input in order to automatically convert the ephemeris data (such as sun angles) into flows for the solar generator.

evidence_quotes.claim: The process creates an adaptable and interoperable model for rapid change analysis.
evidence_quotes.quote: The main added value of this process is that it allows to define an adaptable and interoperable model. For instance, any change on the mission can be studied almost instantly by regenerating the corresponding ephemeris data.

evidence_quotes.claim: Simulation loop adjusts EPS sizing parameters through multiple runs.
evidence_quotes.quote: S and P parameters (amount of elements in Series and Parallel) are readjusted through multiple runs of simulations, until a satisfactory equilibrium state is reached at the power subsystem level.

evidence_quotes.claim: Pre-development feasibility validation is energy-simulation based, not formal V&V.
evidence_quotes.quote: Test different stars observation plans in order to validate their feasibility in terms of energy stability and potentially revise scientific ambitions and needs accordingly.

evidence_quotes.claim: Battery worst-case survival scenario is simulated using SOC thresholds.
evidence_quotes.quote: This scenario can also be simulated by making the simulation start with an initial SOC of 85% followed by three successive orbits with no illumination ... with a minimal acceptable SOC of 20% in order to keep an energy margin.

evidence_quotes.claim: Tool/model interoperability is a claimed integrability outcome.
evidence_quotes.quote: the interoperability of the different tools and methods, made possible by the standardization of files format, is a real enabler for the concurrent engineering process by making it really easy for each subsystem expert to exchange data and to communicate through engineering models.

notes_for_consistency: Single supporting paper focused on a CNES concurrent-engineering workflow and Opalis EPS simulation for one 16U nanosatellite use case. It mentions MBSE as context but does not report SysML, Cameo, Capella, OpenMBEE, PLM, or a formal MBSE reference model. Venue is not reported in the paper text. Formal limitations and formal V&V/test-procedure modeling are not reported; reliability and reproducibility outcomes are not explicit.
